caption: Sites in the insular cortex where electrical stimulation evoked pain in 14 patients, plotted on a sagittal MRI. Most sites sit in the upper posterior part of the insula, and the lower panels sort them by body part and by pain quality.
notice: The pain sites cluster toward the back of the insula, and because the electrode current caused the sensation this points to a cause, not just a correlation.

caption: Sagittal and coronal brain sections with the subgenual prefrontal cortex labeled and a t-value color scale; the strongest values, in red and orange, sit at the subgenual region.
notice: Look at where the peak color falls: it is centered on the subgenual region, which ties the group difference in mood disorders to this spot, a correlation.

caption: A map of the human striatum in which each voxel is colored by the cerebral network it is most strongly connected to; the cortical network colors are shown at the bottom.
notice: Different parts of the striatum take different colors, so each part couples to a different cortical network; this is functional connectivity, a correlation of activity.

caption: Lesion overlap map for 14 middle cerebral artery stroke patients with neglect, shown on axial slices; the colors show how many patients' lesions covered each voxel.
notice: The overlap is deepest in the parietal region, so damage there goes with neglect; lesions point to a cause.

caption: Bar graph of the deficits found at the bedside in patients with cerebellar lesions, with a severity score for each functional category such as executive function, reasoning, calculation and affect.
notice: The tallest bars are executive function, reasoning, calculation and affect, so cerebellar damage produced problems in thinking and mood, not just movement; lesions show cause.

caption: Sagittal slices of an ALE map pooling 691 foci from general semantic contrasts across studies; yellow and red mark places where activation foci agreed.
notice: The large bright patch in the left posterior inferior parietal region in the top row shows that many studies of meaning activate it, a correlation.

caption: Polar angle map from one subject's hemisphere on the inflated surface, with a flattened patch around the occipital pole at right; the colors follow the visual field angle each spot responds to.
notice: The colored angle bands run together in the patch at the occipital pole, which is where the visual areas meet; this is a mapped correlation with the visual field.

caption: Outlines of the lesions (white) of four patients with topographical disorientation, drawn on a structural MRI.
notice: All four white lesions lie in the retrosplenial area behind the corpus callosum, so damage there went with getting lost, and lesions point to a cause.

caption: Group-average map of regions that responded more to human voices than to energy-matched non-vocal sounds, shown on sagittal and axial brain slices of both hemispheres.
notice: The colored patches run along the temporal lobe on both sides, so voice-selective activity lines up with this sulcus region; this is imaging, a correlation.

caption: Mean fMRI activation in extrastriate visual areas of two monkeys under normal conditions (blue), after a V1 lesion (red), and after a V1 lesion plus LGN inactivation (green).
notice: The green bars drop to near zero, so silencing the LGN removed the activation that remained without V1; this is a manipulation, so it shows cause.
